title: DeepRoute Usage Ledger & Per-Path Console Walkthrough
summary: Redwood AE and SE walked Trajectory Labs through the Console's per-route usage ledger, trajectory/flow visualizations, and cost breakdown. Key asks: granular per-path attribution, model variant fallbacks cost impact, and security docs (SOC2, SSO/KMS). Agreed pilot: 30-day sandbox with telemetry, followed by dedicated sizing if perf checks out.
next_steps: Redwood to share SOC2 + SSO/KMS security packet (Maya) by 2026-12-18
Provision 30-day sandbox tenant and demo data (Luis) by 2026-12-20
Trajector y to send sample traffic traces (Samir) by 2026-12-22
Follow-up call to present pilot results and cost model on 2027-01-12 (all)
action_items: Maya Chen: send security pack (SOC2, ISO, KMS integration notes) - due 2026-12-18
Luis Ortega: set up sandbox tenant + sample dashboard with customer's data slices - due 2026-12-20
Samir Gupta: provide 3 days worth of route traces and model mix - due 2026-12-22
Ellie Zhao: confirm pilot budget and PO path - due 2026-12-29
transcript:
Meeting header:
- Date/Time: 2026-12-16 15:00 UTC
- Duration: ~48 minutes
- Attendees: Maya (Redwood AE), Luis (Redwood SE), Anika (CSM), Jared (CTO), Priya (Head ML), Samir (Platform), Ellie (Finance)

AUTO-SUMMARY (auto): quick console walkthrough focused on per-route ledger and cost decomposition; agreement to run 30-day sandbox pilot.

[00:00] Maya (Redwood): hey everyone, thanks for joining, i'll kick us off. um this call is to show the console views for per-route usage and the ledger we call the "deeproute usage ledger", and how you can map token spend back to product routes and models.
[00:18] Jared (Trajectory): hey thanks, yeah we want to see how we can answer finance-level questions like which product flows are burning the most cost and why.
[00:25] Luis (Redwood SE): cool, i'll share my screen. excuse any blur, sometimes the Conzul share is a bit laggy. right now i'm on the routes page — i want to point out the flow map on the left, which we call the trajectory view. it groups requests by route id and shows upstream call chains.
[00:48] Priya: can you filter by model variant? we run a/b between gpt-like open models and a quantized on-prem one.
[00:55] Luis: yes — filter by model label at the top. note model variants are attached to routes, and the ledger keeps the per-token attribution even when we do automatic fallbacks. sometimes transcripts show k-v cache as "keev cache" in logs, but it's the same thing — prefix cache reductions show up in the ledger as negative token deltas.
[01:24] Maya: quick qualification, what's your current stack? samir?
[01:28] Samir: we have a mix — user-facing web app calling a router lambda, then calls to internal microservices that fan out to a few LLM endpoints. everything's in GCP, some sensitive workloads are in an on-prem cluster behind a VPC.
[01:44] Ellie: finance wants to map spend to product lines and to get alerts if a route spikes beyond a threshold.
[01:51] Luis: right, alerts come from the Console — you can set per-route SLOs for token burn or latency. i'll pull up the cost breakdown panel.
[02:05] [screen shows LEDGER table] Luis: here is the usage ledger — each row is a route + model combo, timestamped shards, with tokens in, tokens out, delta, and a cost column that applies your active price sheet. i want to show the trajectory filter so you can see the flows that lead to the top spenders.
[02:28] Priya: how granular does the ledger get? session-level? user-level?
[02:32] Luis: you can do route-level, session-id, and we also materialize short lived per-req traces for up to 30 days in the managed tier, or longer if you buy extended retention. beware that PII fields are redacted automatically unless you configure a retention exception.
[02:54] Jared: is there attribution for cached tokens? we use prefix caching heavily.
[02:59] Maya: good question — the ledger includes cache hits as reduced token usage; we show a "cache savings" line item per route. we've seen customers reduce billed tokens by 20-40% after enabling prefix/KV caching.
[03:15] Priya: are the cache savings calculated from telemetry or inferred?
[03:19] Luis: telemetry — the runtime annotates requests with KV cache hit metrics. small caveat: some of the low-level names in the export become a bit mangled, e.g., KV cache might appear as KV_keev in auto transcripts.
[03:34] Samir: about private workloads — can you keep the control plane in our VPC? we need to ensure keys never leave HSM.
[03:40] Maya: yes, Redwood Private supports customer KMS and HSM integrations; we can run the control plane in your VPC or on-prem. i'll attach the KMS integration doc in the follow-up.
[03:52] Ellie: SOC2? we require SOC2 plus ISO for vendor onboarding.
[03:56] Maya: we are SOC two compliant and have ISO certs — will send the pack.
[04:03] Luis: switching back to the console — here's the cost decomposition for a selected route. top shows token spend split by model (base vs quantized), middle shows infra delta (if you run dedicated capacity), and bottom shows adjustments for batching and cache.
[04:22] Priya: can we simulate different batching strategies to see cost impact?
[04:26] Luis: yes, in Optimize we have a "simulator" that uses your observed sequence length and throughput distribution to estimate token/sec and cost under different batch sizes and quant profiles. i'll show a sample later in the sandbox.
[04:38] [05:00] Jared: another ask: when a route falls back to a cheaper model, can we see the quality regression metrics?
[05:06] Luis: yes — we integrate evals at the prompt-set level. when you configure model fallbacks, we produce a quality delta metric based on your eval set and show it next to cost savings. it's all in the rollout tab.
[05:22] Priya: that sounds critical — we need to maintain NPS on generation quality while optimizing cost.
[05:27] Maya: noted.
[05:30] [06:00] Luis: jumping to anomalies — the console surfaces per-route anomalies using change point detection on token burn and latency. you can drill into the ledger rows and see raw request traces.
[06:19] Samir: how often is the telemetry exported? near-real-time?
[06:23] Luis: streaming with sub-second counters for latency and token counters, consumer-facing dashboards update in ~1s for top-line metrics, ledger granularity is batched per minute for export efficiency.
[06:38] Jared: do you support tagging for internal chargeback? we want to tag by product, team, and customer segment.
[06:44] Maya: yes, route tags map to chargeback groups. you can export per-tag invoice lines into CSV or push to BigQuery via connector.
[06:54] Ellie: does the console provide predicted monthly burn? finance would like a rolling forecast.
[06:59] Luis: we have a forecast panel — it uses recent trajectory and seasonal adjustments to forecast spend and highlights routes with the fastest growth. it's in the billing insights tab.
[07:14] [08:00] Priya: security again — SSO, SAML, role-based access?
[07:18] Maya: we support SSO/SAML, OIDC, and granular RBAC. audit logs are shipped to your SIEM; we can also enable immutable audit snapshots for compliance reviews.
[07:30] Samir: any limitations on per-route retention in Private?
[07:33] Maya: Private customers control retention — you can keep full traces on-prem up to your storage limits. hosted has default 30-day retention unless you buy extended.
[07:45] [12:00] Luis: demoing a sample drill-in — selecting a high-cost route called "/generate/editorial". look at the split: 65% tokens on model-v2, 20% infra (dedicated GPU premium), 15% cache misses leading to regen. See the mini-trace on the right; timestamps show the fan-out to secondary reranker.
[08:17] Priya: what's the reranker cost — is it billed separately?
[08:21] Luis: yes if it's a separate route or model combo; ledger rows are additive so you can attribute reranker cost to the upstream route by enabling request lineage.
[08:30] Jared: can we tag reranker as a shared service and split cost across product teams?
[08:34] Maya: yes, shared services can be split by configured ratios or dynamic attribution based on traffic origin.
[08:40] [18:00] Luis: small note about pricing sheets — the console applies your active price sheet which can include committed discounts for Dedicated pools and model-specific unit pricing. when a route triggers fallback, the ledger shows both observed cost and hypothetical cost had fallback not occurred.
[09:22] Ellie: that hypothetical cost view is great for showback to execs.
[09:26] Luis: exactly.
[09:30] Priya: if we do the sandbox pilot, will we get the Optimize suggestions surfaced automatically?
[09:35] Luis: yes sandbox will run Optimize heuristics and provide batching + quant recommendations and an expected % cost reduction. those are simulation-based but use your real telemetry.
[09:46] Maya: action items recap in a sec — any other blockers?
[09:50] Jared: just one more — latency SLOs are critical for critical flows; how does the Console help with SLO ops?
[09:56] Luis: the routes page ties latency percentiles to the same ledger rows; if a route crosses a latency SLO, we can trigger weighted fallback to cheaper variants or scale dedicated pools depending on policy. you get a timeline of SLO breaches alongside cost.
[10:15] Priya: what's the expected timeline to validate performance under our traffic?
[10:19] Maya: usually for a 30-day sandbox we do a 2-week ingest of telemetry, then run a 1-week stress benchmark with a sample subset. we can size Dedicated after that based on P50/P95 throughput targets.
[10:33] [20:00] Luis: demo wrap-up — here's a share link to an example ledger CSV and a screenshot of the trajectory flow with route filters applied. note: some of the auto transcripts in the console export might label Luis as "Lewis" — it's a small OCR quirk we've seen.
[10:55] Ellie: thanks, please send the SOC docs and the sandbox invite.
[11:00] Maya: will do. we'll also include a short runbook for chargeback exports.
[11:06] Jared: great, looking forward to the sandbox.
[11:09] Maya: recap of next steps: send security pack, provision sandbox, Samir to upload traces, follow-up 2027-01-12. thanks everyone.
[11:20] End of meeting.
